title: Bengal lets state employees draw salary in advance through a digital platform
dek: Short-term advances of up to half a month's pay are interest-free if repaid within 60 days; longer advances can be repaid over up to five years.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal's government employees will be able to draw part of their salary in advance through a digital platform, under a new West Bengal Salary Advance Scheme notified by the state Finance Department, the Millennium Post reported.

The scheme is meant to help employees meet emergencies such as medical bills, children's education or unexpected household costs without turning to high-interest loans from outside lenders, according to the report. It covers regular state government employees in Groups A to D and equivalent posts.

There are two options. A short-term advance of up to half a month's salary must be repaid within the same or the next salary cycle, and in no more than 60 days; it carries no interest, processing fee or platform fee if repaid on time. A multi-month advance, for larger planned spending, can be repaid in instalments over 2 to 60 months, but not beyond the employee's retirement date. The report did not give the interest rate or fees for the longer option.

The notification also raises the ceiling on the advance for buying a motorcycle, scooter or electric two-wheeler to Rs 1.20 lakh, or five months' basic pay or the vehicle's cost if either is lower.

The report did not give the notification's number or date, the name of the platform, or how employees can apply. The Declaration could not find the notification on the Finance Department's website.

sources.title: Millennium Post: Bengal opens salary advance window for employees
